location.en: Your studio apartment, phone call to Brightway
location.zh: 你的套房，打電話到 Brightway

goal.en: Call to follow up on your interview, thank the team, and send what they need.
goal.zh: 打電話追蹤面試結果、向對方道謝，並提供對方需要的資料。

background: small studio apartment with a desk by the window, an open laptop, a phone charger and a closed notebook, a potted plant on the sill, rainy afternoon light

intro.en: Eight days have passed since your second interview. Ms. Wong said they would decide that week, but your inbox is still empty.
intro.zh: 第二次面試已經過了八天。王經理說那週就會決定，但你的信箱還是空空的。

intro.en: You practice your first line twice, then dial Rachel's number.
intro.zh: 你把第一句話練習了兩遍，然後撥了瑞秋的電話。

lines.en: Good morning, Brightway. This is Rachel speaking.
lines.zh: 早安，這裡是 Brightway，我是瑞秋。

choices.en: Hi, it's Kai. So, did I pass or not? Nobody has told me anything.
choices.zh: 嗨，我是凱。所以我到底有沒有過？都沒人跟我說。

lines.en: Um, hello to you too, Kai.

story.en: You sound like a student calling about test scores. Rachel stays polite, but her voice gets a little cooler.
story.zh: 你聽起來像打電話查成績的學生。瑞秋還是很有禮貌，但語氣冷淡了一些。

fail.why: 一開口就問「有沒有過」又抱怨沒人通知，聽起來很沒耐心。先表明身分和來意：Hi Rachel, this is Kai. I'm calling to follow up on my interview.。

choices.en: Hello, I am Kai. I call to ask about the interview last week.
choices.zh: 你好，我是凱。我打來問上週面試的事。

lines.en: Sorry... Kai? Which interview do you mean?
lines.zh: 抱歉……凱？你是說哪一場面試？

story.en: Rachel needs a few seconds to figure out who you are and why you're calling. A clear first line would have saved you both the trouble.
story.zh: 瑞秋花了好幾秒才搞懂你是誰、為什麼打來。第一句說清楚，就能省下這些麻煩。

fail.why: 講電話自報姓名說 This is Kai，不說 I am Kai；說明這通電話的目的要用進行式 I'm calling to...，I call 聽起來像平常的習慣。說 I'm calling to follow up on my interview.。

choices.en: Hi Rachel, this is Kai. I'm calling to follow up on my interview.
choices.zh: 嗨，瑞秋，我是凱。我打來追蹤一下面試的結果。
choices.tip: This is Kai. 是電話中自報姓名的說法，再用 I'm calling to follow up on... 一句說清楚來意。

lines.en: Oh, hi Kai! Thanks for calling. Ms. Wong hasn't made a final decision yet.
lines.zh: 喔，嗨，凱！謝謝你打來。王經理還沒做最後決定。

lines.en: She's been away this week, visiting a hotel client.
lines.zh: 她這週出差，去拜訪一家飯店客戶。

choices.en: What? She said this week! So that means I didn't get it, right?
choices.zh: 什麼？她說這週的！所以意思是我沒上，對吧？

lines.en: No, it means she's busy. Please don't jump to conclusions.
lines.zh: 不是，意思是她很忙。請不要急著下結論。

story.en: You turned a simple delay into bad news. Rachel spends the next minute calming you down instead of talking about the job.
story.zh: 你把單純的延誤當成了壞消息。瑞秋接下來一分鐘都在安撫你，而不是談工作。

fail.why: 對方說還沒決定，就急著質問、往壞處想，聽起來很焦躁。冷靜地問時間：Do you know when she might make a decision?。

choices.en: No problem. Do you know when she might make a decision?
choices.zh: 沒問題。你知道她大概什麼時候會決定嗎？
choices.tip: Do you know when...? 用間接問句客氣地探問時間，不會給對方壓力。

choices.en: Oh, which hotel? I've always wanted to try a fancy hotel buffet.
choices.zh: 喔，哪間飯店？我一直很想吃高級飯店的自助餐。

lines.en: I... can't really share client details. Was there something else?
lines.zh: 我……不太方便透露客戶資訊。還有其他事嗎？

story.en: You called about a job and ended up asking about a buffet. Rachel politely steers you back, but the moment is gone.
story.zh: 你打來問工作，結果問起了自助餐。瑞秋禮貌地把話題拉回來，但氣氛已經不對了。

fail.why: 追蹤電話要聚焦在面試進度，不要被對方的一句話帶到別的話題。可以問：Do you know when she might make a decision?。

lines.en: She should decide by Friday. Is there anything else I can help with?
lines.zh: 她應該星期五前會決定。還有什麼我可以幫忙的嗎？

choices.en: Yes. Could you help me say some good words to Ms. Wong?
choices.zh: 有，可以幫我在王經理面前說些好話嗎？

lines.en: Some... good words? Like what, hello and thank you?
lines.zh: 一些……好的字？像是你好和謝謝嗎？

story.en: Rachel isn't sure if you want a favor or a vocabulary list. Either way, HR can't really help with that.
story.zh: 瑞秋搞不清楚你是要她幫忙，還是要一張單字表。不管是哪個，人資都不方便幫這種忙。

fail.why: 「說好話」直譯成 say good words 英文聽不懂，道地說法是 put in a good word for me。不過請人資關說並不恰當，這時應該道謝：I wanted to thank you for setting up both interviews.。

choices.en: Yes, I wanted to thank you for setting up both interviews.
choices.zh: 有，我想謝謝你幫我安排了兩次面試。
choices.tip: I wanted to thank you for + V-ing，用過去式 wanted 語氣比 I want 更客氣。

choices.en: Yes. I want to thank you for arrange both of my interviews.
choices.zh: 有，我想謝謝你幫我安排兩次面試。

lines.en: Oh! For arranging them? You're welcome, I think.
lines.zh: 喔！你是說安排面試嗎？應該……不客氣？

story.en: Your thank-you comes out a little tangled, and Rachel isn't sure what she's being thanked for. The nice gesture gets lost in grammar.
story.zh: 你的道謝說得有點打結，瑞秋不太確定你在謝什麼。一番好意就這樣卡在文法裡。

fail.why: thank you for 後面接名詞或動名詞：thank you for arranging...。改用過去式 I wanted to thank you for... 會更委婉有禮。

lines.en: That's very kind of you. Oh, actually, Ms. Wong asked to see some of your product photos.
lines.zh: 你真貼心。對了，王經理說想看看你拍的商品照。

choices.en: Of course! I will send them to you with the fastest speed.
choices.zh: 當然！我會用最快的速度寄給你。

lines.en: The fastest speed? Um, today is fine, Kai.
lines.zh: 最快的速度？呃，凱，今天寄就可以了。

story.en: Rachel pictures you racing across town with a box of photos. It's just an email, so any speed will do.
story.zh: 瑞秋腦中浮現你抱著一箱照片衝過大街小巷的畫面。其實只是寄封電子郵件，什麼速度都行。

fail.why: 「用最快的速度」直譯成 with the fastest speed 很不自然，英文說 as soon as possible，或直接給時間：I can email you a link to my portfolio this afternoon.。

choices.en: Of course. I will send to you this afternoon by email.
choices.zh: 當然。我今天下午會用電子郵件寄給你。

lines.en: Send... what to me? The photos?

story.en: Your sentence forgot to say what you're sending. Rachel waits for the rest, but it never comes.
story.zh: 你的句子忘了說要寄什麼。瑞秋等著你說完，但後半句一直沒出現。

fail.why: send 後面要接受詞，不能省略：send them to you。中文說「寄給你」可以不提東西，英文不行。可以說 I can email you a link to my portfolio this afternoon.。

choices.en: Sure. I can email you a link to my portfolio this afternoon.
choices.zh: 當然，我今天下午可以寄作品集的連結給你。
choices.tip: 給出明確時間（this afternoon）比 soon 更讓人安心。portfolio 是作品集。

lines.en: Perfect. I'll make sure she sees them. Thanks for calling, Kai.
lines.zh: 太好了，我會確保她看到。凱，謝謝你打來。

choices.en: Thank you, Rachel. I look forward to hearing from you.
choices.zh: 謝謝你，瑞秋。期待你們的消息。
choices.tip: I look forward to hearing from you. 是追蹤電話和信件最常見的結尾，look forward to 後面接 V-ing。

choices.en: Sorry for disturbing you! Really, so sorry for calling. Sorry!
choices.zh: 打擾你了！真的很抱歉打來，對不起！

lines.en: You don't need to apologize. Following up is completely normal.
lines.zh: 你不需要道歉，追蹤進度是很正常的事。

story.en: You apologized three times for a polite, normal phone call. Rachel starts to wonder what you did wrong.
story.zh: 一通禮貌又正常的電話，你道歉了三次。瑞秋開始懷疑你是不是做錯了什麼。

fail.why: 台灣人習慣說「不好意思打擾了」，但英文道歉太多次，會讓人以為你真的做錯事。追蹤面試很正常，用期待收尾：Thank you, Rachel. I look forward to hearing from you.。

choices.en: Okay. If I don't hear anything by Friday, I'll call every day.
choices.zh: 好。如果星期五前沒消息，我就每天打。

lines.en: Please don't. We'll call you when there's news.
lines.zh: 請不要這樣。有消息我們會打給你。

story.en: Rachel quietly writes 'calls a lot' next to your name. That is not the note you were hoping for.
story.zh: 瑞秋默默在你的名字旁邊寫下「很常打來」。這可不是你期待的評語。

fail.why: 說要每天打電話，聽起來像在施壓。追蹤一次就夠了，最後用期待收尾：I look forward to hearing from you.。

lines.en: Following up like this was a nice touch. Talk soon, Kai!
lines.zh: 像這樣打來追蹤很加分喔。凱，再聊！

story.en: You hang up feeling calm. Two days later, your phone rings again. This time, the screen says: Ms. Wong.
story.zh: 掛上電話，你覺得安心多了。兩天後，你的手機又響了。這次螢幕上顯示：王經理。

notes.en: I'm calling to follow up on...
notes.explain: follow up on 是「追蹤、跟進」某件事的進度。打電話時先自報姓名（This is Kai.），再用這句說明來意。

example.en: Hi, this is Kai. I'm calling to follow up on my application.
example.zh: 嗨，我是凱。我打來追蹤一下我的應徵進度。

notes.en: I wanted to thank you for...
notes.explain: 用過去式 wanted 比 I want 委婉。for 後面接名詞或 V-ing，例如 thank you for your time、thank you for setting up the interview。

example.en: I wanted to thank you for your time last week.
example.zh: 我想謝謝你上週撥空和我見面。

notes.explain: 中文「我寄給你」可以不說寄什麼，英文的 send 一定要有受詞：send it to you、send you the link。

example.en: I'll send you the link this afternoon.
example.zh: 我今天下午把連結寄給你。

notes.en: say good words / with the fastest speed
notes.explain: 「說好話」是 put in a good word for someone；「用最快的速度」是 as soon as possible。另外，面試後請人資幫忙說好話並不恰當。

example.en: I'll get it to you as soon as possible.

notes.explain: 超過對方說的時間還沒消息，打一次電話或寄一封信追蹤很常見，也顯示你有興趣。不需要一直道歉，也不要天天打。

example.en: I look forward to hearing from you.
